text:
kevin: Anyone have quick sizing guidance for a Private/VPC POC? Customer is fintech (eu-west-1), wants a 3-month trial. Target: ~120 concurrent active sessions, spikes to 300. Mix of models: 7B/13B for most traffic, occasional 34B for high-accuracy cases. SLO: p50 latency <300ms for short prompts. Need recommended GPU counts, node sizes, NVMe, and a ballpark monthly cost.

maria: Quick calc to start: assume avg prompt 150 tokens, avg completion 80 tokens, ~2 interactions/min per session.
kevin: math?
maria: tokens/min = 120 sessions * (150+80) * 2 = 55,200 tokens/min => ~920 tokens/sec sustained. Spikes to 300 sessions => ~2,300 tok/sec.
aj: throughput per GPU (approx, on A100-80GB): 7B ~300 tok/s, 13B ~120 tok/s, 34B ~35-45 tok/s (depends on quant/kv cache). For our mixed workload baseline (majority 13B/7B) use the 13B numbers for conservative sizing.
aj: To hit ~1,000 tok/s sustained: 13B at 120 tok/s => ~9 GPUs. Add 20% buffer => 11-12 GPUs. For spike headroom (2,300 tok/s) we can either autoscale to ~20 GPUs or route heavy requests to a cheaper async queue / smaller model.
maria: Recommended starting fleet for the POC: 12x A100-80GB (or equivalent A10G/RTX6000 if cost constraints, but perf will be lower). Node spec: 1 GPU per node or 2 GPUs per node depending on NIC/PCIe topology. Per node (2x GPU) suggestion: 96 vCPU, 512GB RAM, 4TB NVMe local for shard/cache, 2x 25Gbps NIC.
lisa: Ops notes: prefer 1 GPU per host for easier thermal/power distribution in customer racks if they are constrained. If customer wants density, 2 GPUs/host with good airflow is ok. For VPC deployments also recommend 10Gbps+ peering to our control plane for telemetry and updates.
kevin: autoscaling strategy?
lisa: Start with manual reserved capacity (12 GPUs), enable scale-up policy based on tokens/sec and queue depth. Use a fast-path route to 7B pool for non-critical completions to preserve latency. For spikes >95th percentile route to fallback async queue with webhook callback.
ops-bot: Cost sketch (amortized + ops): 12x A100-80 (~$2,500/node/mo amortized hardware) => $30,000/mo. Hosts + networking + support + SW ops => +$6k/mo. Total rough POC run-rate: ~$36k/mo. If customer buys rack up-front we can provide adjusted amortization.
kevin: can we reduce cost for POC?
aj: yes: start with 8 GPUs (8x A100) and throttle heavy 34B calls to smaller model or async. Also enable mixed-precision quant and KV cache warmup to cut per-token cost. Consider using cheaper GPU types in eu-west for non-peak hours.
maria: I'll draft a one-page hardware sizing & onboarding checklist for the customer that includes these numbers, thermal/power checklist, recommended manifest, and a short config snippet for node pool.
kevin: please include a short example manifest we can hand to the customer's infra team.
maria: snippet below — just illustrative: 
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: gp-a100-80gb
spec:
  replicas: 6   # starts with 12 GPUs as 2x per node, or set to 12 for 1x per node
  resources:
    gpu: nvidia.com/gpu: 2
    cpu: 96
    memory: 512Gi
    localNVMe: 4Ti
  labels:
    region: eu-west-1
    workload: private-llm
```

lisa: add note to ask customer for rack power (kW per rack) and available PDU density. Also confirm their firewall rules for outbound control-plane endpoints.
kevin: perfect — can you push the one-pager and the cost options (8gpu/12gpu/20gpu) into the partner repo? I'll loop in AE and customer infra. :thumbsup:
maria: on it, will have draft by EOD.
